# Process Brief: PM-12 Define Scope
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent) on behalf of Agno JF

## Selection

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Project | Lead Lab |
| Primary process | PM-12 Define Scope |
| Performance domain | Scope |
| Focus area | Planning |
| Disposition | Required |
| Rigor | Formal |
| Scope authority | PM or authorized sponsor; not named in current records |
| Final launch authority | LeadLab Director |
| Trigger | After PM-11 requirements analysis and before PM-13 structure or custom-app commitment |

## Purpose

Define the proposed Lead Lab web-app boundaries, deliverables, exclusions, assumptions, constraints, and success measures so the PM can decide what is committed for the September program and what remains deferred.

## Why This Process Is Required

- The current canonical platform and backlog still describe WordPress.
- The new plan proposes a custom web app with features beyond the original SharePoint replacement.
- PM-11 identified launch-critical requirements, proposed enhancements, and unresolved decisions.
- The project needs an explicit boundary before work is decomposed and estimated.
- The launch fallback depends on knowing which capabilities are truly required.

## Tailoring Factors

| Factor | Project assessment | Scope effect |
|---|---|---|
| Criticality | Scope determines whether the September program can launch safely. | Define acceptance conditions and fallback boundaries explicitly. |
| Scale | One community and one initial program. | Use a focused MVP scope statement rather than a platform-wide product scope. |
| Duration | Delivery window is short and fixed. | Separate launch scope from post-launch options and apply a feature freeze. |
| Complexity | Platform change, authentication, content, files, events, security, and operations interact. | Record assumptions, constraints, dependencies, and exclusions. |
| Requirements maturity | Core replacement needs are evidenced; new app features remain proposed. | Do not convert proposed requirements into commitments without authority. |
| Governance | LeadLab Director is final launch approver; PM/scope approver is not named. | Keep the proposed baseline visible and flag missing approval. |

## Minimum Scope Output

The PM-12 output must contain:

- Scope statement and product boundary.
- In-scope deliverables and capabilities.
- Explicit exclusions and deferred capabilities.
- Assumptions and constraints.
- External dependencies and required inputs.
- Success measures and acceptance boundary.
- Fallback boundary if the custom app is not ready.
- Approval authority and baseline status.

## Planned Scope Alternatives

The draft should show two boundary options:

1. **Replacement MVP:** Original portal capabilities plus only the technical controls needed for a safe self-hosted app.
2. **Skool-inspired MVP:** Replacement MVP plus community, classroom, calendar, roles, and moderation features proposed in the delivery plan.

The options are not a decision. The PM and LeadLab Director must determine which boundary is committed for the September program.

## Planned Process Sequence

| Sequence | Process | Dependency |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | PM-12 Define Scope | Establishes proposed boundaries and deliverables. |
| 2 | PM-13 Develop Scope Structure | Decomposes the approved boundary into work packages or backlog items. |
| 3 | PM-14 Monitor and Control Scope | Controls approved scope after delivery begins. |
| 4 | PM-15 Validate Scope | Confirms completed work against approved acceptance conditions. |

## Open Inputs for Stage 02

- PM decision on replacement-only versus Skool-inspired MVP boundary.
- Approval authority and scope owner.
- Platform-direction decision and application environment.
- Authentication and participant-data decision.
- Required September content and acceptance conditions.
- Launch fallback boundary and feature freeze date.
